name: [WEEKLY] Public-Facing App Auth-Bypass to Server-Side Code Execution (web-server process spawning a shell/interpreter)
description: Detects a web-application or appliance service process (httpd, nginx, php-fpm, w3wp, java/tomcat, node, or VMware vpxd) directly spawning an OS shell, scripting interpreter, or download/recon LOLBin — the universal post-exploitation tell after a pre-auth or auth-bypass flaw is turned into code execution. This matters this fortnight because a cluster of critical public-facing-app bypass and RCE disclosures landed together: vBulletin pre-auth eval() RCE (CVE-2026-61511) now has a public exploit, VMware vCenter auth-bypass + directory-traversal RCE and ESX VM-escape (CVE-2026-59309/59310/47876), plus a wave of GHSA auth-bypass advisories (LightRAG hardcoded DEFAULT_TOKEN_SECRET CVE-2026-61740, Auth.js fail-open GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3, Budibase cross-origin credential leak GHSA-mqhr-6j6h-74p5, @better-auth/scim provider-id collision GHSA-rjg6-39jm-rgg4) — all sharing the T1190 → code-execution/destructive-action chain. It spans the exploit and execution kill-chain stages: the auth check is defeated (exploit) and the server process is coerced into running attacker code (install/actions). It FIRES when an internet-facing service binary is the parent of an interactive shell or interpreter it never legitimately launches; it does NOT fire on normal application workers, CI/build agents, or admin-initiated maintenance scripts whose parent is a login shell or scheduler rather than the network-facing daemon. Reference IOCs (<c2_domain_list>, <sha256_list>) are substitution slots only — the parent/child process relationship is the durable signal.
query: Image:(*httpd* OR *apache2* OR *nginx* OR *php\-fpm* OR *php\-cgi* OR *php* OR *w3wp.exe* OR *java* OR *java.exe* OR *node* OR *node.exe* OR *tomcat.exe* OR *catalina.sh* OR *vmware\-vpxd* OR *vpxd*)
